findings.title: Participant structural properties are not applied during updates
findings.why_it_matters: The public update_element path accepts participant properties such as blackBox and processRef, but only the generic properties map is changed. The participant's structural processRef field and process-root lifecycle remain unchanged, so converting a white-box pool to black-box leaves a process root and processRef in exported BPMN, while setting processRef on a black-box pool has no effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Either reject structural participant properties in update_element or implement an atomic participant update that validates processRef/blackBox, synchronizes the participant field, creates/removes owned process roots and contents safely, and persists the result.
evidence: src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:237-253 merges update.properties and assigns only element.properties; no participant.processRef or document.processes update occurs.
src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:242-250 serializes participant.processRef, not properties.processRef, so properties.processRef is ignored and properties.blackBox cannot remove a processRef.
Reproduction: create a white-box participant, updateElement(..., {properties:{blackBox:true}}), then export; the participant still has its original processRef and the generated process root remains.
src/server/tools.ts exposes update_element with an unrestricted properties object, making this reachable through the MCP surface.
